Definition: akin to G4579; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb):--move.
BiblicalUsage: In Greek, saínō means to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), that is (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb). It stands in 1 Thessalonians 3:3: "…no man should be moved by these afflictions…" — in the SBL text the verb stands as σαίνομαι.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe saínō is in the Bible for a reason, and even one mention is enough for God.
